_comment: Manifest for the installed artefact imx500_network_efficientdet_lite0_pp.rpk (imx500-models 1:1.0.0-1).
Machine-measured 2026-09-05 on station rpi-turret: sha256 over the file, and
inference_rate/task/labels read out of the metadata JSON embedded in the .rpk
itself. license is the imx500-models copyright file's entry for this artefact.
Re-measure and re-review after any package upgrade - §9.3 exists so a changed
artefact stops startup instead of changing what 'person' means mid-run.
layout. The .rpk metadata does not declare them, so §9.2's probe is the
bbox_order, bbox_normalized and the output layout were measured on 2026-09-05 and are
no longer provisional. row_layout/output_tensors describe the four-tensor on-sensor
output; a package upgrade that changes the firmware layout is caught at startup by §9.3
only if the manifest is re-verified — rerun the probe + a sample capture before trusting
notes: sha256 and inference_rate_hz=23 measured from the artefact on 2026-09-05; labels resolved
the artefact's own metadata declares cpu.bbox_normalization = true and a 1:1 input aspect
ratio - the only layout fields evidenced by the file rather than by the probe.
320x320 is this export's published input size; if the device reports otherwise the
adapter adopts the device's value and records a warning instead of guessing twice.
A 320x320-class input sees a person as roughly 20x60 pixels at moderate range: §36's
measurement_quality and §37.1's selectability floor are what keep that from being
mistaken for a good lock, not the detector score alone.

Measured on this station 2026-09-05: on-sensor PP output is four tensors (boxes (100,4), scores (100,), classes (100,), count (1,)); boxes are yxyx in the 320x320 NETWORK-INPUT PIXEL space, not normalized — the .rpk's declared 'bbox_normalization' refers to the compiled model's coordinate handling, not the output scale, and output values up to ~314 are what settle the question.
